record.context_brief: Topology dependence of the McShane integral
record.original_question: Let f: Ω → X be a function on a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ) with values in a Banach space X. If T_1 and T_2 are two topologies on Ω for which μ is quasi-Radon, and f is McShane integrable with respect to T_1, must f also be McShane integrable with respect to T_2?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.8 (Fremlin, [56]). Let f: Ω → X be a function defined in a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ) and taking values in a Banach space X. Let T_1 and T_2 be two topologies on Ω for which μ is quasi-Radon. Suppose f is McShane integrable with respect to T_1. Is f McShane integrable with respect to T_2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ be a complete probability space and let $X$ be a Banach space. Recall that a topology $\mathcal{T}$ on $\Omega$ is said to make $\mu$ quasi-Radon if $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu, \mathcal{T})$ is a quasi-Radon measure space, i.e., $\mathcal{T} \subseteq \Sigma$, $\mu$ is inner regular with respect to closed sets, $\mu$ is $\tau$-additive (the measure of the union of any upward-directed family of open sets equals the supremum of their measures), and the measure is complete and locally determined.

For such a quasi-Radon structure, a function $f: \Omega \to X$ is called McShane integrable (with respect to $\mathcal{T}$) with integral $w \in X$ if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a "gauge" $\Delta: \Omega \to \mathcal{T}$ with $x \in \Delta(x)$ for all $x \in \Omega$, such that for every finite collection $\{(E_1, x_1), \ldots, (E_n, x_n)\}$ with the $E_i \in \Sigma$ pairwise disjoint, $x_i \in \Omega$, $E_i \subseteq \Delta(x_i)$, and $\sum_{i=1}^n \mu(E_i) \geq 1 - \varepsilon$, one has
$$\Big\| \sum_{i=1}^n \mu(E_i)\, f(x_i) - w \Big\| \leq \varepsilon.$$

Suppose $\mathcal{T}_1$ and $\mathcal{T}_2$ are two topologies on $\Omega$ each making $\mu$ quasi-Radon, and suppose $f: \Omega \to X$ is McShane integrable with respect to $\mathcal{T}_1$. Must $f$ also be McShane integrable with respect to $\mathcal{T}_2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by Fremlin, appears to remain open in general. A partial affirmative answer is known: if one of the topologies has a countable base, then McShane integrability transfers between the two topologies and the integrals agree. No full resolution was located in the search results.

status_evidence.title: The McShane integral in weakly compactly generated spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Affirmative answer when T_1 has a countable base; integrals coincide.
status_evidence.claim: A partial positive answer is known under the additional assumption of a countable base on one topology.
